unit.title: How agents work: the loop, tools and memory

lesson.title: Inside the loop
lesson.subtitle: The one text an agent reads and writes, and why its loop needs a stop

chapters.label: The loop in code, and its stop

scenes.visual: A list: Where’s its plan?; One long text; Let’s open it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A colleague asked me: where does an agent keep its plan, its tool calls and its memory? The answer surprises people. It’s all one long text. Let’s open it up.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: inside the loop, one text at a time.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: <|tools|>weather route reminder …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Darsi Tiny reads one text, top to bottom. Small markers split it into parts: the tools that are on, your request, its plan, its call, the result. Each marker is a single token, and nobody can fake one by typing it.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The model writes three kinds of part: the plan, the call and the answer. The app writes everything else: the tools line, your request and every result. After a call, the model stops and waits.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: The loop: the app adds text
scenes.narration: So the loop is the app, adding to one text. It sends the text so far, and the model writes a call. The app runs the tool and adds the result. Then it sends the text again, until the model answers.

scenes.visual: A list: Call: route, Kafi to Dala; Result: 70 km; Call: weather in Dala; Only then: the answer.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Ask for the trip from Kafi to Dala, and the text grows twice. First a route call, and its result: seventy kilometres. Then a weather call for Dala, and its result. Only then does Darsi Tiny write the answer.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! After Darsi Tiny writes a weather call, who writes the result into the text?

scenes.visual: A list: The app writes every result; The model stops after a call; Its own result = invented data.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The app, from the tool. Darsi Tiny was trained to stop after a call and wait. A model that wrote its own result would be inventing data, so a good app never allows it.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: As code, the loop is only a few lines. Here the model is scripted: a stand-in that returns what a model would write. The code asks for the next part, and stops at an answer.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But what if the model never answers? It could call the same tool again and again, and the loop would run forever, using battery and data. So real agents have a step limit, then stop and tell the person.

scenes.visual: A list: Open “What it sees”; Press One step; Watch the text grow; Kafi to Dala: count calls.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: inside an agent’s loop
scenes.narration: In the app, open What Darsi Tiny sees, then press One step. Watch the text grow: plan, call, result, answer. Then run the trip from Kafi to Dala, and count the calls.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. My agent keeps calling the weather tool, and never answers. What should the app have?

scenes.visual: Summary points: One text, with markers; The model writes; the app adds results; Every loop needs a stop.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: One text, with markers · The model writes; the app adds results · Every loop needs a stop
scenes.narration: A step limit, so the loop stops and tells a person. Remember: it’s all one text, with markers. The model writes plans, calls and answers, and the app adds the results. And every loop needs a stop.

scenes.visual: A list: One conversation on a paper strip; Model parts in blue; App parts in green; Where would the app check?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: write one agent conversation on a long paper strip. Model parts in blue, app parts in green. Then ask: which colour can make mistakes, and where would the app check?

checkpoints.prompt: After Darsi Tiny writes a weather call, who writes the result into the text?

options.text: Darsi Tiny, from what it learned
The app, from the weather tool

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the app runs the tool and adds its result. The model stops after a call and waits, so it never invents a result.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the model never writes a result. The app runs the tool and adds what it returned.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent keeps calling the weather tool and never answers. What should the app have?

options.text: A step limit that stops the loop and tells a person

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a step limit stops a loop that would run forever, and hands the problem to a person.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a bigger model or a faster phone can still loop forever. The app needs a limit that stops it.
